q: 10 मई 1857 को 1857 के विद्रोह की औपचारिक शुरुआत एक व्यापक सैनिक क्रांति के रूप में किस सैन्य छावनी से हुई?
e: Although Mangal Pandey of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry fired the first shot at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857, the organized Revolt of 1857 formally began at Meerut on 10 May 1857 when sepoys marched to Delhi and proclaimed Bahadur Shah Zafar as Emperor of Hindustan. (यद्यपि मंगल पांडे ने 29 मार्च 1857 को बैरकपुर में विद्रोह किया, 1857 की संगठित क्रांति 10 मई 1857 को मेरठ छावनी से प्रारंभ हुई।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Immediate cause: greased cartridges (cow and pig fat) of the new Enfield P-53 rifle; (2) Governor-General during 1857: Lord Canning; British PM: Lord Palmerston; (3) Symbol of the 1857 Revolt: Lotus and Chapati; (4) Bahadur Shah Zafar was exiled to Rangoon (Burma), where he died in 1862.
qe: On 10 May 1857, the Revolt of 1857 formally broke out as a full-scale sepoy uprising from which military cantonment?

q: अपने अल्पवयस्क पुत्र बिरजिस कादिर की ओर से लखनऊ (अवध) में 1857 के विद्रोह का नेतृत्व किसने किया था?
e: Begum Hazrat Mahal led the uprising in Lucknow from June 1857 until Sir Colin Campbell recaptured the city in March 1858, after which she took refuge in Nepal. (बेगम हज़रत महल ने जून 1857 से लखनऊ में विद्रोह का नेतृत्व किया और अंततः नेपाल चली गईं।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Major UP centres & leaders: Kanpur (Nana Saheb & Tatya Tope), Jhansi (Rani Lakshmibai), Faizabad (Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah), Bareilly (Khan Bahadur Khan), Allahabad (Maulvi Liaquat Ali), Baghpat (Shah Mal); (2) In Bihar (Jagdishpur), 80-year-old Zamindar Kunwar Singh led the revolt; (3) Sir Hugh Rose suppressed the Jhansi revolt and called Rani Lakshmibai "the only man among the rebels".
qe: Who led the Revolt of 1857 in Lucknow (Awadh) on behalf of her minor son Birjis Qadr?

q: किस क्रांतिकारी लेखक ने 1909 में प्रकाशित अपनी प्रसिद्ध पुस्तक में 1857 के विद्रोह को "भारत का प्रथम स्वतंत्रता संग्राम" कहा?
e: Vinayak Damodar Savarkar authored *The Indian War of Independence of 1857* (1909), hailing it as the First War of Indian Independence. (वी.डी. सावरकर ने 1909 में प्रकाशित अपनी पुस्तक में 1857 के विद्रोह को 'भारत का प्रथम स्वतंत्रता संग्राम' कहा।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) R.C. Majumdar famously wrote: "Neither first, nor national, nor a war of independence"; (2) S.N. Sen (*Eighteen Fifty-Seven*, 1957) was the official historian appointed by the Government of India; (3) Benjamin Disraeli called it a "National Revolt" in the British Parliament; (4) Sir John Lawrence & Seeley dismissed it as a "Sepoy Mutiny".
qe: Which revolutionary author described the Revolt of 1857 as the "First War of Indian Independence" in his famous book published in 1909?

q: 1 नवंबर 1858 को लॉर्ड कैनिंग ने ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी से ब्रिटिश क्राउन को भारत का शासन हस्तांतरित करने वाला महारानी विक्टोरिया का घोषणापत्र किस शहर में पढ़ा था?
e: Following the Government of India Act, 1858, Lord Canning (India's first Viceroy) read Queen Victoria's Proclamation at Minto Park, Allahabad (Prayagraj) on 1 November 1858. (1 नवंबर 1858 को लॉर्ड कैनिंग ने इलाहाबाद (प्रयागराज) के मिंटो पार्क में महारानी विक्टोरिया का घोषणापत्र पढ़ा।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) The 1858 Act abolished the Court of Directors & Board of Control, creating the Secretary of State for India (first: Lord Stanley) assisted by a 15-member Council of India; (2) Doctrine of Lapse was formally abandoned and Indian princes were assured of non-annexation; (3) Allahabad served as the capital of North-Western Provinces for one day/period after 1858.
qe: On 1 November 1858, Lord Canning read out Queen Victoria's Proclamation—transferring India's administration from the East India Company to the British Crown—at which city?

q: 1857 के विद्रोह के तुरंत बाद भारतीय सेना के पुनर्गठन (यूरोपीय व भारतीय सैनिकों का अनुपात बढ़ाने) हेतु किस ब्रिटिश आयोग का गठन किया गया था?
e: The Peel Commission (1858–59) recommended reorganizing the Indian Army on 'divide and counterpoise' lines: raising the European-to-Indian ratio to 1:2 in Bengal and 1:3 in Madras/Bombay, placing artillery strictly under European control, and recruiting 'martial races' (Sikhs, Gurkhas, Pathans). (पील आयोग की सिफारिश पर भारतीय सेना का पुनर्गठन किया गया, यूरोपीय सैनिकों का अनुपात बढ़ाया गया और तोपखाना यूरोपीयों के अधीन रखा गया।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Recruitment from Awadh, Bihar, and Central India (the 1857 epicentre) was drastically curtailed; (2) Strachey Commission (1880) dealt with Famine; (3) Fraser Commission (1902) dealt with Police reforms.
qe: Which British Commission was appointed immediately after the Revolt of 1857 to reorganize the Indian Army (increasing the ratio of European to Indian soldiers)?

q: 1857 में फैजाबाद (अयोध्या) के किस तेजस्वी विद्रोही नेता पर अंग्रेजों ने ₹50,000 का इनाम घोषित किया था और उन्हें अपना सबसे कट्टर व साहसी शत्रु माना?
e: Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah ('Danka Shah') led the 1857 Revolt in Faizabad/Awadh, defeated British forces at Chinhat (June 1857), and carried a ₹50,000 British bounty before being treacherously killed by the Raja of Powayan in June 1858. (मौलवी अहमदुल्ला शाह ने फैजाबाद में 1857 के विद्रोह का नेतृत्व किया और अंग्रेजों ने उन पर ₹50,000 का इनाम रखा था।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Maulvi Liaquat Ali led the revolt in Allahabad (Prayagraj); (2) Azimullah Khan was Nana Saheb's chief advisor; (3) General Bakht Khan commanded the rebel forces in Delhi.
qe: Who was the fiery rebel leader of Faizabad (Ayodhya) in 1857, originally from Madras, on whom the British placed a bounty of ₹50,000 and whom they called their "best and bravest soldier" among enemies?

q: कौन-से प्रसिद्ध उर्दू शायर दिल्ली में 1857 के विद्रोह और उसके भीषण दमन के प्रत्यक्षदर्शी थे, जिन्होंने अपनी पीड़ा 'दस्तंबू' में दर्ज की?
e: Mirza Asadullah Khan Ghalib (1797–1869, born in Agra, lived in Delhi) witnessed the 1857 Revolt and British reprisal firsthand and recorded it in his Persian diary *Dastanbuy*. (मिर्ज़ा गालिब दिल्ली में 1857 की क्रांति के प्रत्यक्षदर्शी थे और उन्होंने इसका विवरण 'दस्तंबू' में लिखा।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Bahadur Shah Zafar himself was a gifted Urdu poet under the pen name 'Zafar'; (2) Sir Syed Ahmad Khan wrote *Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind* (*Causes of the Indian Revolt*, 1859) analyzing the 1857 uprising.
qe: Which Urdu poet was an eyewitness to the Revolt of 1857 and its brutal aftermath in Delhi, vividly recording his grief in his letters and diary 'Dastanbuy'?

q:
सूची-I (1857 विद्रोह केंद्र) को सूची-II (दमनकर्ता ब्रिटिश अधिकारी) से सुमेलित कीजिए और सही कूट चुनिए:
सूची-I: (1) दिल्ली, (2) कानपुर, (3) झाँसी, (4) इलाहाबाद व बनारस
सूची-II: (a) सर ह्यूरोज़, (b) कर्नल नील, (c) जॉन निकलसन व हडसन, (d) सर कॉलिन कैंपबेल
e: Delhi — John Nicholson (killed during storming) & Lt. Hudson (1-c); Kanpur (and Lucknow) — Sir Colin Campbell (2-d); Jhansi & Gwalior — Sir Hugh Rose (3-a); Allahabad & Banaras — Colonel James Neill (4-b). (दिल्ली-निकलसन/हडसन, कानपुर-कॉलिन कैंपबेल, झाँसी-ह्यूरोज़, इलाहाबाद-कर्नल नील; अतः 1-c, 2-d, 3-a, 4-b।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Jagdishpur (Bihar) was suppressed by William Taylor and Vincent Eyre; (2) Tatya Tope (Ramchandra Pandurang) waged guerrilla warfare until betrayed by Man Singh and hanged at Shivpuri in April 1859.
qe:
Match List-I (1857 Revolt Centre) with List-II (British Commander who suppressed it) and select the correct code:
List-I: (1) Delhi, (2) Kanpur, (3) Jhansi, (4) Allahabad & Banaras
List-II: (a) Sir Hugh Rose, (b) Colonel Neill, (c) John Nicholson & Hudson, (d) Sir Colin Campbell

q: निम्नलिखित में से किस वर्ग/समूह ने अंग्रेजों के प्रति निष्ठावान या तटस्थ रहने के बजाय 1857 के विद्रोह में सक्रिय रूप से भाग लिया?
o: ग्वालियर के सिंधिया तथा हैदराबाद के निज़ाम
अवध के बेदखल ताल्लुकदार एवं किसान
इंदौर के होलकर तथा पटियाला के सिख शासक
e: Dispossessed Taluqdars (hurt by the Summary Settlement of 1856 after Awadh's annexation) and overburdened peasants of Awadh formed the mass backbone of the 1857 Revolt, whereas Scindia, Nizam, Holkar, Patiala, and the Western-educated intelligentsia largely stayed loyal or aloof. (अवध के बेदखल ताल्लुकदार और किसान 1857 के विद्रोह की मुख्य शक्ति थे, जबकि सिंधिया, निज़ाम, होलकर और शिक्षित मध्यम वर्ग विद्रोह से दूर रहे।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Lord Canning remarked that the loyal Indian princes acted as "breakwaters to the storm"; (2) After 1858, the British restored Taluqdari rights in Awadh to win over feudal landlords.
qe: Which of the following classes/groups actively SUPPORTED the Revolt of 1857 rather than remaining aloof or loyal to the British?
oe: Scindia of Gwalior and Nizam of Hyderabad
Dispossessed Taluqdars and peasants of Awadh
Holkar of Indore and Sikh rulers of Patiala

q: अपनी ऐतिहासिक पुस्तक 'पॉवर्टी एंड अन-ब्रिटिश रूल इन इंडिया' (1901) में प्रसिद्ध 'धन का निष्कासन सिद्धांत' (Drain of Wealth) किसने प्रतिपादित किया?
e: Dadabhai Naoroji ('Grand Old Man of India') first articulated the Drain of Wealth Theory in his 1867 paper *England's Debt to India* and elaborated it in *Poverty and Un-British Rule in India* (1901). (दादाभाई नौरोजी ने सर्वप्रथम 'धन का निष्कासन सिद्धांत' प्रतिपादित किया, जिसे उन्होंने 'अनिष्टों का अनिष्ट' कहा।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Romesh Chunder Dutt authored *The Economic History of India* (1902); (2) The 1896 Calcutta Session of INC officially adopted the Drain of Wealth Theory; (3) Dadabhai Naoroji was the first Indian elected to the British House of Commons (1892, Finsbury Central) and presided over INC thrice (1886, 1893, 1906).
qe: Who propounded the famous 'Drain of Wealth Theory' (धन का निष्कासन सिद्धांत) in his landmark work *Poverty and Un-British Rule in India* (1901)?

q: किस ब्रिटिश भू-राजस्व व्यवस्था के अंतर्गत लगान का बंदोबस्त सीधे व्यक्तिगत किसान (रैयत) के साथ किया गया, जो ब्रिटिश भारत के लगभग 51% क्षेत्र (मद्रास व बंबई) में लागू थी?
e: The Ryotwari System—piloted by Captain Alexander Read in Baramahal (1792) and formally introduced by Sir Thomas Munro in Madras (1820) and Elphinstone in Bombay—dealt directly with individual ryots (peasants) without Zamindar intermediaries. (थॉमस मुनरो व अलेक्जेंडर रीड द्वारा लागू रैयतवाड़ी व्यवस्था में सीधे किसान से भू-राजस्व लिया जाता था और यह ~51% क्षेत्र में थी।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Area coverage: Ryotwari (~51%), Mahalwari (~30%), Permanent Settlement (~19%); (2) Izaredari (revenue farming) was introduced by Warren Hastings in 1772; (3) Though intermediary-free on paper, Ryotwari had exorbitant revenue rates (50%–55%) causing peasant indebtedness.
qe: Under which British land revenue system was the settlement made directly with the individual cultivator (peasant), covering approximately 51% of British India (Madras & Bombay Presidencies)?

q: उत्तर-पश्चिमी प्रांत (उ.प्र.), पंजाब और मध्य भारत में लागू 'महालवाड़ी व्यवस्था' (1822)—जिसमें संपूर्ण ग्राम समुदाय (महाल) सामूहिक रूप से लगान के लिए उत्तरदायी था—का सूत्रपात किसने किया?
e: Holt Mackenzie proposed the Mahalwari System in 1819 (enacted via Regulation VII of 1822), and it was later revised and operationalized by Robert Merttins Bird ("Father of Land Settlements in Northern India") and James Thomason in 1833. (हॉल्ट मैकेंज़ी ने 1822 में महालवाड़ी व्यवस्था प्रारंभ की तथा आर.एम. बर्ड (1833) ने इसे सुव्यवस्थित किया।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Under Bird's 1833 scheme, the state share was initially 66% of rental value, later reduced to 50% by the Saharanpur Rules (1855) under Lord Dalhousie; (2) Permanent Settlement (1793) covered Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, and Varanasi division of UP.
qe: Who formulated the 'Mahalwari System' (1822) of land revenue—in which the entire village community (Mahal) was jointly responsible for revenue—implemented across North-Western Provinces (UP), Punjab, and Central India?

q: भारत के हथकरघा बुनकरों के विनाश (अनौद्योगीकरण) पर 1834 में किस ब्रिटिश गवर्नर-जनरल ने प्रसिद्ध टिप्पणी की थी: "व्यापार के इतिहास में ऐसी दुर्दशा की शायद ही कोई मिसाल मिले। भारतीय मैदान कपास बुनकरों की हड्डियों से सफेद हो रहे हैं"?
e: Governor-General Lord William Bentinck wrote this stark observation in 1834 as machine-made Lancashire textiles flooded duty-free into India under the Charter Act of 1813 (ending EIC's trade monopoly) while Indian textiles faced heavy tariffs in Britain. (लॉर्ड विलियम बेंटिंक ने 1834 में भारतीय हथकरघा उद्योग के विनाश पर यह मार्मिक टिप्पणी की थी।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) One-way free trade transformed India from the world's largest exporter of finished cotton textiles into an exporter of raw materials (cotton, indigo, jute, opium) and importer of British manufactures; (2) First modern cotton textile mill in India was set up by Cowasjee Nanabhoy Davar in Bombay in 1854; (3) First jute mill was set up at Rishra (Bengal) in 1855.
qe: Which British historian and Governor-General famously remarked in 1834 about the deindustrialization of India's handloom weavers: "The misery hardly finds a parallel in the history of commerce. The bones of the cotton-weavers are bleaching the plains of India"?

q: 1793 के लॉर्ड कॉर्नवालिस के स्थायी बंदोबस्त से संबंधित 'सूर्यास्त कानून' (Sunset Law) क्या था?
o: किसानों को सूर्यास्त पर खेती बंद करनी होती थी
निर्धारित तिथि के सूर्यास्त तक लगान जमा न करने पर जमींदार की जमींदारी नीलाम कर दी जाती थी
सूर्यास्त के बाद कलकत्ता बंदरगाह से जहाज नहीं जा सकते थे
नील कारखानों को सूर्यास्त तक बंद करना होता था
e: Under the Sunset Law of 1794, if a Zamindar failed to pay the fixed revenue installment (10/11th to Company, 1/11th kept by Zamindar) before sunset on the stipulated date, his zamindari was immediately confiscated and auctioned. (सूर्यास्त कानून के तहत तय तिथि के सूर्यास्त तक भू-राजस्व जमा न करने पर जमींदार की जमींदारी नीलाम कर दी जाती थी।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) This led to the rise of absentee landlordism and sub-infeudation (Patnidars); (2) Bengal Tenancy Act, 1885 was later passed to give limited protection to occupancy tenants.
qe: What was the 'Sunset Law' (सूर्यास्त कानून) associated with Lord Cornwallis's Permanent Settlement of 1793?
oe: Peasants had to stop farming at sunset
If a Zamindar failed to deposit fixed revenue by sunset of the due date, his estate was auctioned
Trade ships could not leave Calcutta port after sunset
Indigo factories had to close by sunset

q: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा 'होम चार्जेज' (गृह व्यय) का हिस्सा नहीं था, जो भारत से ब्रिटेन को धन के निष्कासन का प्रमुख घटक था?
o: भारत में सेवारत/सेवानिवृत्त ब्रिटिश अधिकारियों के वेतन एवं पेंशन
लंदन में लिए गए सार्वजनिक ऋण पर ब्याज तथा ब्रिटिश रेलवे पूँजी पर गारंटीड ब्याज
लंदन स्थित इंडिया ऑफिस का व्यय
बंगाल के भारतीय किसानों को दी जाने वाली प्रत्यक्ष कृषि सब्सिडी
e: 'Home Charges' comprised London India Office expenses, British officers' salaries/pensions/furloughs, interest on Sterling debt & guaranteed railway returns (5% assured return to British investors), and military stores—NEVER agricultural subsidies to Indian peasants. (होम चार्जेज में लंदन स्थित इंडिया ऑफिस व्यय, ब्रिटिश अधिकारियों के वेतन-पेंशन व रेलवे गारंटीड ब्याज शामिल थे, भारतीय किसानों की सब्सिडी नहीं।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Under the 'Old Guarantee System' (1849–69), British railway investors received a guaranteed 5% annual return paid from Indian tax revenues; (2) TISCO (Tata Iron and Steel Company) was founded by Jamsetji Tata at Sakchi (Jamshedpur) in 1907.
qe: Which of the following was NOT a component of the 'Home Charges' (गृह व्यय) that formed a major part of the Drain of Wealth from India to Britain?
oe: Salaries and pensions of British civil and military officials serving/retired from India
Interest on public debt raised in London and guaranteed interest on British railway capital
Expenses of the India Office in London
Direct agricultural subsidies paid to Indian farmers in Bengal

q: ब्रिटिश आर्थिक शोषण के विरुद्ध 19वीं सदी के किसान आंदोलनों और उनके क्षेत्रों का निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा युग्म सही सुमेलित नहीं है?
e: The Moplah (Mappila) Rebellion occurred in the MALABAR region of KERALA (NOT Gujarat). All other three pairs are correctly matched. (मोपला विद्रोह केरल के मालाबार क्षेत्र में हुआ था, गुजरात में नहीं।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Indigo Revolt (1859–60) was led by Digambar Biswas & Bishnu Biswas, depicted by Dinabandhu Mitra in his play *Nil Darpan* (1860); (2) Deccan Riots (1875) against moneylenders led to the Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act, 1879; (3) Eka Movement (1921–22) in Awadh (Hardoi, Bahraich, Sitapur) was led by Madari Pasi.
qe: Which of the following pairs of 19th-century peasant uprisings against British economic exploitation and their regions is NOT correctly matched?

q: इतिहासकार रजनी पाम दत्त ने भारत के ब्रिटिश आर्थिक शोषण को तीन विशिष्ट चरणों में विभाजित किया है। उनका सही कालानुक्रम क्या है?
o: वाणिज्यिक पूँजीवाद → औद्योगिक पूँजीवाद → वित्तीय पूँजीवाद
औद्योगिक पूँजीवाद → वाणिज्यिक पूँजीवाद → वित्तीय पूँजीवाद
वित्तीय पूँजीवाद → वाणिज्यिक पूँजीवाद → औद्योगिक पूँजीवाद
वाणिज्यिक पूँजीवाद → वित्तीय पूँजीवाद → औद्योगिक पूँजीवाद
e: In *India Today* (1940), R.P. Dutt outlined: (1) Mercantile/Commercial Capitalism (1757–1813: EIC monopoly & direct plunder), (2) Industrial Capitalism (1813–1858: free-trade market for British goods & deindustrialization), and (3) Finance Capitalism (1858–1947: British capital investment in railways, plantations, banks, and mines). (सही क्रम: वाणिज्यिक पूँजीवाद (1757–1813) → औद्योगिक पूँजीवाद (1813–1858) → वित्तीय पूँजीवाद (1858–1947)।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Charter Act of 1813 ended EIC's monopoly over Indian trade (except tea and China trade); (2) Charter Act of 1833 abolished EIC's commercial activities completely.
qe: Historian Rajani Palme Dutt divided British economic exploitation of India into three distinct phases. What is their correct chronological sequence?
oe: Mercantile Capitalism (1757–1813) → Industrial Capitalism (1813–1858) → Finance Capitalism (1858–1947)
Industrial Capitalism → Mercantile Capitalism → Finance Capitalism
Finance Capitalism → Mercantile Capitalism → Industrial Capitalism
Mercantile Capitalism → Finance Capitalism → Industrial Capitalism

q: "वेदों की ओर लौटो" के प्रेरक नारे के साथ 1875 ई. में बंबई में 'आर्य समाज' की स्थापना किसने की थी?
e: Swami Dayananda Saraswati (original name: Mool Shankar, born in Tankara, Gujarat) founded Arya Samaj in Bombay in April 1875 (headquarters shifted to Lahore in 1877) and authored *Satyarth Prakash* in Hindi. (स्वामी दयानंद सरस्वती ने 1875 में बंबई में आर्य समाज की स्थापना की और 'सत्यार्थ प्रकाश' की रचना की।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Dayananda was the first to use the term 'Swaraj' and advocate Hindi as India's national language; (2) After his death (1883), Dayananda Anglo-Vedic (DAV) College was founded at Lahore (1886, Lala Hansraj) and Gurukul Kangri at Haridwar (1902, Swami Shraddhanand); (3) Arya Samaj launched the Shuddhi movement and opposed caste rigidity, child marriage, and idol worship.
qe: Who founded the 'Arya Samaj' in Bombay in 1875 with the inspiring slogan "Go Back to the Vedas" (वेदों की ओर लौटो)?

q: 1873 ई. में पुणे में 'सत्यशोधक समाज' की स्थापना किसने की और जाति-विरोधी प्रसिद्ध पुस्तक 'गुलामगिरी' की रचना की?
e: Mahatma Jyotirao Phule founded Satyashodhak Samaj on 24 September 1873 in Pune to fight Brahmanical orthodoxy and uplift backward castes and women; he published *Gulamgiri* in 1873 (dedicated to the American anti-slavery movement). (ज्योतिराव फुले ने 1873 में पुणे में सत्यशोधक समाज की स्थापना की तथा 'गुलामगिरी' लिखी।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Jyotirao Phule and Savitribai Phule (India's first female school teacher) opened India's first girls' school at Bhide Wada, Pune in 1848; (2) Periyar founded the Self-Respect Movement (1925) in Tamil Nadu; (3) Sree Narayana Guru (Kerala) gave the motto "One Caste, One Religion, One God for Mankind".
qe: Who founded the 'Satyashodhak Samaj' (Truth-Seekers' Society) in Pune in 1873 and authored the seminal anti-caste work *Gulamgiri*?

q: अपने आध्यात्मिक गुरु श्री रामकृष्ण परमहंस की स्मृति में 1 मई 1897 को बेलूर (कलकत्ता के निकट) में 'रामकृष्ण मिशन' की स्थापना किसने की?
e: Swami Vivekananda (original name: Narendranath Datta, born 12 January 1863 — National Youth Day) founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897 to combine Vedantic spirituality with selfless social service ("Service to Man is Service to God"). (स्वामी विवेकानंद ने 1897 में बेलूर में रामकृष्ण मिशन की स्थापना की।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Vivekananda delivered his historic speech at the World's Parliament of Religions in Chicago on 11 September 1893; (2) Subhas Chandra Bose called Vivekananda the "Spiritual Father of the Modern Nationalist Movement"; (3) Sister Nivedita (Margaret Noble) was his prominent Irish disciple; (4) He published *Prabuddha Bharata* (English) and *Udbodhana* (Bengali).
qe: Who founded the 'Ramakrishna Mission' on 1 May 1897 at Belur (near Calcutta) in memory of his spiritual guru Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa?

q: केशव चंद्र सेन की प्रेरणा से 1867 ई. में बंबई में 'प्रार्थना समाज' की स्थापना किसने की, जिसे बाद में न्यायमूर्ति एम.जी. रानाडे व आर.जी. भंडारकर ने लोकप्रिय बनाया?
e: Dr. Atmaram Pandurang founded Prarthana Samaj in Bombay in 1867 focusing on monotheism, widow remarriage, women's education, and abolition of caste rigidity. (डॉ. आत्माराम पांडुरंग ने 1867 में बंबई में प्रार्थना समाज की स्थापना की।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) M.G. Ranade ('Socrates of Maharashtra') also founded the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1870) and Indian National Social Conference (1887); (2) Gopal Hari Deshmukh was famous as 'Lokahitawadi'; (3) D.K. Karve founded India's first Women's University (SNDT) in 1916; (4) Pandita Ramabai founded Arya Mahila Samaj and Sharada Sadan.
qe: Who founded the 'Prarthana Samaj' in Bombay in 1867 (inspired by Keshab Chandra Sen), later popularized by Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade and R.G. Bhandarkar?

q: सर सैयद अहमद खान ने 1875 ई. में अलीगढ़ में 'मुहम्मडन एंग्लो-ओरिएंटल (MAO) कॉलेज' की स्थापना की, जो किस वर्ष अलीगढ़ मुस्लिम विश्वविद्यालय (AMU) बना?
e: MAO College (founded 1875) was elevated to Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) by an Act of Parliament in 1920. (1875 में स्थापित MAO कॉलेज वर्ष 1920 में अलीगढ़ मुस्लिम विश्वविद्यालय (AMU) बना।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Sir Syed founded the Scientific Society (Ghazipur 1864, moved to Aligarh) and published the reformist journal *Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq*; (2) In contrast to the modernist Aligarh Movement, the orthodox Deoband Movement (Darul Uloom Deoband, Saharanpur, UP) was founded in 1866 by Muhammad Qasim Nanautavi and Rashid Ahmad Gangohi; (3) Banaras Hindu University (BHU) was founded by Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya in 1916.
qe: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the 'Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental (MAO) College' at Aligarh in 1875, which later became Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) in which year?

q: किस समाज सुधारक के अथक प्रयासों के परिणामस्वरूप ब्रिटिश सरकार ने 'हिंदू विधवा पुनर्विवाह अधिनियम, 1856' पारित किया?
e: Principal of Sanskrit College, Calcutta, Pandit Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar cited Vedic/Shastric authority to campaign for widow remarriage, leading to the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856 (drafted under Dalhousie, enacted under Canning). (ईश्वर चंद्र विद्यासागर के प्रयासों से 1856 का हिंदू विधवा पुनर्विवाह अधिनियम पारित हुआ।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Behramji Malabari's efforts led to the Age of Consent Act, 1891 (raising girl's consent age from 10 to 12); (2) Harbilas Sarda's efforts led to the Child Marriage Restraint Act (Sarda Act, 1929 — minimum marriage age 14 for girls, 18 for boys); (3) Keshab Chandra Sen's efforts led to the Native Marriage Act, 1872.
qe: Which social reformer's tireless campaign led the British Government to enact the 'Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act (Act XV of 1856)'?

q: 1875 में न्यूयॉर्क में 'थियोसोफिकल सोसायटी' की स्थापना किसने की, जिसका अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मुख्यालय 1882 में अड्यार (मद्रास) स्थानांतरित किया गया?
o: मैडम एच.पी. ब्लावात्स्की एवं कर्नल एच.एस. ओल्कॉट
e: Madame Helena Petrovna Blavatsky (Russian) and Colonel Henry Steel Olcott (American) founded the Theosophical Society in New York in 1875 and moved its headquarters to Adyar (Madras) in 1882. (मैडम ब्लावात्स्की व कर्नल ओल्कॉट ने 1875 में न्यूयॉर्क में थियोसोफिकल सोसायटी की स्थापना की और 1882 में अड्यार में मुख्यालय बनाया।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Annie Besant joined in 1889, came to India in 1893, became President of Theosophical Society in 1907, and founded Central Hindu College at Banaras in 1898 (which became the nucleus of BHU in 1916); (2) Henry Vivian Derozio led the radical 'Young Bengal Movement' at Hindu College, Calcutta (1826–31).
qe: Who established the 'Theosophical Society' in New York (1875) and later shifted its international headquarters to Adyar (Madras) in 1882?
oe: Annie Besant and Allan Octavian Hume
Sister Nivedita and Charles Freer Andrews
Madame H.P. Blavatsky and Colonel H.S. Olcott

q:
सूची-I (संगठन) को सूची-II (संस्थापक) से सुमेलित कीजिए और सही कूट चुनिए:
सूची-I: (1) तत्वबोधिनी सभा (1839), (2) सर्वेंट्स ऑफ इंडिया सोसायटी (1905), (3) राधास्वामी सत्संग (1861), (4) भारत धर्म महामंडल (1902)

e: Tattvabodhini Sabha (1839) — Devendranath Tagore (1-c); Servants of India Society (1905, Pune) — Gopal Krishna Gokhale (2-a); Radha Soami Satsang (1861, Agra) — Shiv Dayal Saheb (3-d); Bharat Dharma Mahamandala (1902, Varanasi) — Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya (4-b). (तत्वबोधिनी सभा-देवेंद्रनाथ टैगोर, सर्वेंट्स ऑफ इंडिया-गोखले, राधास्वामी सत्संग-शिवदयाल साहेब, भारत धर्म महामंडल-मालवीय; अतः 1-c, 2-a, 3-d, 4-b।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Brahmo Samaj split in 1866 into Adi Brahmo Samaj (Devendranath Tagore) and Brahmo Samaj of India (Keshab Chandra Sen), and again in 1878 forming Sadharan Brahmo Samaj (Ananda Mohan Bose & Shibnath Shastri); (2) Dev Samaj (1887, Lahore) was founded by Shiv Narayan Agnihotri.

Match List-I (Organization) with List-II (Founder) and select the correct code:

q:
'धर्म सभा' (1830) और 'आत्मीय सभा' (1815) के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: राजा राममोहन राय ने एकेश्वरवाद के प्रचार और मूर्तिपूजा व जातिगत कठोरता के विरोध हेतु 1815 में कलकत्ता में आत्मीय सभा की स्थापना की।
कथन II: राधाकांत देव ने पारंपरिक हिंदू प्रथाओं की रक्षा और सती प्रथा उन्मूलन के विरोध हेतु 1830 में रूढ़िवादी धर्म सभा की स्थापना की।
उपर्युक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?
o: कथन I और कथन II दोनों
न तो कथन I और न ही कथन II
e: Both statements are historically accurate. Interestingly, despite opposing Sati abolition, Radhakanta Deb actively supported Western education and female education in Bengal. (दोनों कथन सत्य हैं; राममोहन राय ने 1815 में आत्मीय सभा तथा राधाकांत देव ने 1830 में धर्म सभा की स्थापना की।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Raja Ram Mohan Roy wrote *Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin* (Gift to Monotheists, 1809 in Persian) and *Precepts of Jesus* (1820); (2) Mughal Emperor Akbar II conferred the title 'Raja' on Ram Mohan Roy in 1830; he died at Bristol (England) in 1833.
qe:
Consider the following statements regarding the 'Dharma Sabha' (1830) and 'Atmiya Sabha' (1815):
Statement I: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Atmiya Sabha in Calcutta in 1815 to propagate monotheism and oppose idolatry and caste rigidities.
Statement II: Radhakanta Deb founded the orthodox Dharma Sabha in 1830 to defend traditional Hindu practices and oppose the abolition of Sati.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
oe: Both Statement I and Statement II
Neither Statement I nor Statement II

q: 1913 ई. में सैन फ्रांसिस्को (अमेरिका) में 'ग़दर पार्टी' की स्थापना किसने की, जिसके प्रथम अध्यक्ष सोहन सिंह भकना थे?
e: Lala Hardayal (along with Sohan Singh Bhakna, Kartar Singh Sarabha, and Bhai Parmanand) founded the Ghadar Party in November 1913 at San Francisco (Yugantar Ashram), publishing the weekly *Ghadar* in Urdu, Punjabi, Hindi, and other languages. (लाला हरदयाल ने 1913 में सैन फ्रांसिस्को में ग़दर पार्टी की स्थापना की।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Shyamji Krishna Varma founded 'India House' (1905) in London and published *The Indian Sociologist*; (2) Madam Bhikaji Cama ("Mother of Indian Revolution") unfurled the first Indian tricolour at Stuttgart (Germany) in August 1907; (3) Komagata Maru incident occurred in 1914 (Baba Gurdit Singh).
qe: Who founded the 'Ghadar Party' in San Francisco (USA) in 1913 with Sohan Singh Bhakna as its first President?

q: 18 अप्रैल 1930 को बंगाल में 'इंडियन रिपब्लिकन आर्मी' के बैनर तले प्रसिद्ध 'चटगाँव शस्त्रागार छापे' का नेतृत्व किसने किया?
e: Schoolteacher Surya Sen ('Masterda'), along with Ganesh Ghosh, Lokenath Bal, Ananta Singh, Pritilata Waddedar, and Kalpana Dutta, executed the daring Chittagong Armoury Raid on 18 April 1930; Surya Sen was hanged on 12 January 1934. (मास्टरदा सूर्य सेन ने 18 अप्रैल 1930 को चटगाँव शस्त्रागार छापे का नेतृत्व किया।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki threw a bomb at Muzaffarpur (1908, targeting Magistrate Kingsford); Khudiram became one of India's youngest martyrs (age 18); (2) Udham Singh assassinated Michael O'Dwyer in London in March 1940 to avenge Jallianwala Bagh; (3) Pritilata Waddedar led the Pahartali European Club raid (1932).
qe: Who led the famous 'Chittagong Armoury Raid' (18 April 1930) in Bengal under the banner of the Indian Republican Army?

q: चापेकर बंधुओं (दामोदर हरि व बालकृष्ण हरि चापेकर) ने 22 जून 1897 को पुणे में किस ब्रिटिश अधिकारी की हत्या कर क्रांतिकारी युग की प्रथम प्रमुख राजनीतिक हत्या की?
o: डब्ल्यू.सी. रैंड (प्लेग कमिश्नर) एवं लेफ्टिनेंट आयर्स्ट
e: Outraged by the brutal house-to-house plague inspection measures in Pune, the Chapekar brothers assassinated Plague Commissioner W.C. Rand and Lt. Ayerst on 22 June 1897. (पुणे में प्लेग के दौरान अत्याचार के विरोध में चापेकर बंधुओं ने 22 जून 1897 को प्लेग कमिश्नर डब्ल्यू.सी. रैंड व ले. आयर्स्ट की हत्या की।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Madan Lal Dhingra assassinated Curzon Wyllie in London in 1909; (2) Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Azad assassinated J.P. Saunders in Lahore (17 Dec 1928) to avenge Lala Lajpat Rai's death; (3) Ras Behari Bose & Basant Kumar Biswas threw a bomb at Viceroy Lord Hardinge in Delhi (Dec 1912).
qe: The Chapekar Brothers (Damodar Hari and Balkrishna Hari Chapekar) carried out India's first major political assassination of the revolutionary era in Pune (22 June 1897) by killing:
oe: W.C. Rand (Plague Commissioner) and Lt. Ayerst

q: 1902 ई. में कलकत्ता में 'अनुशीलन समिति' तथा 1904 ई. में महाराष्ट्र में 'अभिनव भारत सोसायटी' की स्थापना क्रमशः किसने की?
o: बारींद्र कुमार घोष तथा बाल गंगाधर तिलक
अरविंद घोष तथा गोपाल कृष्ण गोखले
e: Pramathanath Mitra (P. Mitra, with Satish Chandra Basu, Jatindranath Banerjee & Barindra Ghosh) founded Anushilan Samiti in Calcutta in 1902, while V.D. Savarkar transformed 'Mitra Mela' (1899) into 'Abhinav Bharat Society' in 1904. (कलकत्ता में अनुशीलन समिति के संस्थापक प्रमथनाथ मित्र (1902) तथा महाराष्ट्र में अभिनव भारत के संस्थापक वी.डी. सावरकर (1904) थे।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Barindra Kumar Ghosh & Bhupendranath Dutta started the revolutionary weekly *Yugantar* (1906); (2) Aurobindo Ghosh was defended by C.R. Das in the Alipore Bomb Conspiracy Case (1908); (3) Pulin Bihari Das founded the Dacca Anushilan Samiti (1905).
qe: Who founded the 'Anushilan Samiti' in Calcutta (1902) and who founded the 'Abhinav Bharat Society' in Maharashtra (1904)?
oe: Barindra Kumar Ghosh and Bal Gangadhar Tilak
Aurobindo Ghosh and Gopal Krishna Gokhale

q: अक्टूबर 1943 में नेताजी सुभाष चंद्र बोस ने 'आज़ाद हिंद की अस्थायी सरकार' (अर्ज़ी हुकूमत-ए-आज़ाद हिंद) की स्थापना और आज़ाद हिंद फौज (INA) का पुनर्गठन किस शहर में किया?
e: On 21 October 1943, Subhas Chandra Bose proclaimed the Provisional Government of Free India in Singapore, giving the famous war cries "Delhi Chalo" and "Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom". (21 अक्टूबर 1943 को सुभाष चंद्र बोस ने सिंगापुर में आज़ाद हिंद की अस्थायी सरकार की स्थापना की।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) INA was originally conceived by Captain Mohan Singh (1942) in Malaya and handed over to Bose by Ras Behari Bose in July 1943; (2) INA had four brigades: Gandhi, Nehru, Subhas, and the women's 'Rani of Jhansi Regiment' (led by Captain Lakshmi Sahgal); (3) Famous Red Fort INA Trials (Nov 1945) tried Shah Nawaz Khan, Prem Kumar Sahgal, and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon (defended by Bhulabhai Desai, Tej Bahadur Sapru, Nehru); (4) Subhas Bose founded the Forward Bloc in May 1939.
qe: In October 1943, Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose established the 'Provisional Government of Free India' (Arzi Hukumat-e-Azad Hind) and reorganized the Indian National Army (INA) in which city?

q: काकोरी ट्रेन एक्शन (9 अगस्त 1925) में चार क्रांतिकारियों को फाँसी दी गई। निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा शहीद और उनके फाँसी स्थल (दिसंबर 1927) का युग्म सही सुमेलित नहीं है?
e: Thakur Roshan Singh was hanged at NAINI JAIL, ALLAHABAD (Prayagraj) on 19 December 1927, NOT Lucknow Jail. All other three pairs are exact: Bismil (Gorakhpur), Ashfaqulla (Faizabad), and Lahiri (Gonda). (ठाकुर रोशन सिंह को 19 दिसंबर 1927 को नैनी जेल, प्रयागराज में फाँसी दी गई थी, न कि लखनऊ जेल में।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) The Kakori action was planned by Hindustan Republican Association (HRA, founded Kanpur 1924 by Sachindra Sanyal, Bismil, Jogesh Chatterjee); (2) Sachindra Sanyal authored the revolutionary textbook *Bandi Jeevan*; (3) Chandra Shekhar Azad evaded arrest at Kakori and later reorganized HSRA (1928); (4) UP Government officially renamed 'Kakori Conspiracy' to 'Kakori Train Action' in August 2021.
qe: Four revolutionaries were sentenced to death in the Kakori Train Action (9 August 1925). Which of the following pairs of martyrs and their place of execution (December 1927) is NOT correctly matched?

q: महात्मा गांधी के लेख 'द कल्ट ऑफ द बॉम्ब' के उत्तर में प्रसिद्ध क्रांतिकारी दस्तावेज़ 'द फिलॉसफी ऑफ द बॉम्ब' (बम का दर्शन, 1930) किसने लिखा था?
e: HSRA ideologue Bhagwati Charan Vohra drafted *The Philosophy of the Bomb* (with inputs from Chandra Shekhar Azad and Yashpal) in January 1930; he was martyred in May 1930 while testing a bomb on the banks of the Ravi river. (HSRA विचारक भगवती चरण वोहरा ने जनवरी 1930 में 'बम का दर्शन' (The Philosophy of the Bomb) लिखा था।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Jatindra Nath Das died on 13 September 1929 after a historic 63-day hunger strike in Lahore Jail demanding political prisoner status; (2) Bhagat Singh wrote *Why I Am an Atheist* in Lahore Central Jail (1930); (3) Durgawati Devi ('Durga Bhabhi') helped Bhagat Singh escape Lahore after the Saunders assassination.
qe: Who authored the famous revolutionary pamphlet *The Philosophy of the Bomb* (1930) in response to Mahatma Gandhi's essay *The Cult of the Bomb*?

q:
निम्नलिखित क्रांतिकारी घटनाओं को सही कालानुक्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए:
1. केंद्रीय विधानसभा बम कांड (भगत सिंह व बटुकेश्वर दत्त)
2. काकोरी ट्रेन एक्शन
3. चटगाँव शस्त्रागार छापा
4. लाहौर में जे.पी. सांडर्स की हत्या
e: Chronology: Kakori Train Action (9 Aug 1925) → Assassination of Saunders (17 Dec 1928) → Central Legislative Assembly Bombing (8 April 1929) → Chittagong Armoury Raid (18 April 1930). Hence 2, 4, 1, 3. (कालानुक्रम: काकोरी (1925) → सांडर्स वध (दिस. 1928) → असेंबली बम कांड (अप्रैल 1929) → चटगाँव छापा (अप्रैल 1930), अतः 2, 4, 1, 3।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru were executed in the Lahore Conspiracy Case on 23 March 1931; (2) First Indian woman to fire at a British Governor (Stanley Jackson, Calcutta Univ. convocation, 1932) was Bina Das.
qe:
Arrange the following revolutionary events in correct chronological order:
1. Central Legislative Assembly Bombing (Bhagat Singh & B.K. Dutt)
2. Kakori Train Action
3. Chittagong Armoury Raid
4. Assassination of J.P. Saunders in Lahore

q: महात्मा गांधी ने 1917 में दमनकारी 'तिनकठिया' नील खेती प्रणाली के विरुद्ध भारत में अपना पहला सत्याग्रह बिहार के किस जिले में प्रारंभ किया?
e: Invited by local peasant Rajkumar Shukla (at the 1916 Lucknow INC Session), Gandhi launched the Champaran Satyagraha (1917)—his first Civil Disobedience in India—forcing abolition of the Tinkathia system (3/20th of land under indigo). (राजकुमार शुक्ल के निमंत्रण पर गांधीजी ने 1917 में बिहार के चंपारण से भारत में अपना पहला सत्याग्रह प्रारंभ किया।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Gandhi's early 3 movements: Champaran (1917, Civil Disobedience), Ahmedabad Mill Strike (Feb–Mar 1918, first Hunger Strike), Kheda Satyagraha (Mar 1918, first Non-Cooperation); (2) Rabindranath Tagore gave Gandhi the title 'Mahatma' after Champaran; (3) Dr. Rajendra Prasad, J.B. Kripalani, Brajkishore Prasad, and Mahadev Desai joined Gandhi in Champaran.
qe: Mahatma Gandhi launched his first Satyagraha in India in 1917 against the oppressive 'Tinkathia' indigo cultivation system in which district of Bihar?

q: 12 मार्च 1930 को महात्मा गांधी ने 78 चुने हुए अनुयायियों के साथ साबरमती आश्रम से ऐतिहासिक 'दांडी मार्च' प्रारंभ किया और किस तिथि को दांडी में नमक कानून तोड़ा?
e: Covering 240 miles (~385 km) in 24 days, Gandhi picked up a handful of natural salt at Dandi (Navsari, Gujarat) on 6 April 1930, formally launching the Civil Disobedience Movement. (24 दिनों की पैदल यात्रा के बाद 6 अप्रैल 1930 को दांडी में नमक कानून तोड़कर सविनय अवज्ञा आंदोलन प्रारंभ हुआ।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) C. Rajagopalachari led the Salt March from Trichy to Vedaranyam in Tamil Nadu; (2) Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan ('Frontier Gandhi') led the 'Khudai Khidmatgar' (Red Shirts) in NWFP; (3) Sarojini Naidu led the Dharasana Salt Works raid (May 1930), reported globally by American journalist Webb Miller; (4) Gandhi attended only the Second Round Table Conference (London, 1931).
qe: On 12 March 1930, Mahatma Gandhi began his historic 'Dandi March' (Salt Satyagraha) with 78 chosen followers from Sabarmati Ashram and broke the salt law at Dandi on:

q: 4 फरवरी 1922 को गोरखपुर जिले (उत्तर प्रदेश) की किस हिंसक घटना के कारण महात्मा गांधी ने असहयोग आंदोलन को तत्काल स्थगित कर दिया?
e: After an angry mob burnt a police station killing 22 policemen at Chauri Chaura (Gorakhpur) on 4 February 1922, Gandhi withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement via the Bardoli Resolution on 12 February 1922. (4 फरवरी 1922 के चौरी-चौरा कांड के बाद गांधीजी ने 12 फरवरी 1922 को बारडोली प्रस्ताव द्वारा असहयोग आंदोलन वापस ले लिया।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Non-Cooperation Movement began on 1 August 1920 (the day Lokmanya Tilak passed away); (2) Following its suspension, C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru formed the 'Swaraj Party' on 1 January 1923 at Allahabad; (3) Mahatma Gandhi presided over ONLY ONE INC Session—Belgaum (Karnataka) in 1924.
qe: Which violent incident on 4 February 1922 in Gorakhpur district (Uttar Pradesh) prompted Mahatma Gandhi to abruptly suspend the Non-Cooperation Movement?

q: 1947 के पश्चात् 560 से अधिक देशी रियासतों के भारतीय संघ में सफल एकीकरण के लिए किसे 'भारत का लौह पुरुष' कहा जाता है?
e: India's first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, aided by States Ministry Secretary V.P. Menon, achieved the peaceful integration of over 560 princely states (his birth anniversary 31 October is National Unity Day). (सरदार वल्लभभाई पटेल ने वी.पी. मेनन के सहयोग से 560+ रियासतों का भारत में एकीकरण किया।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Three tricky states: Junagadh (integrated via Plebiscite, Feb 1948), Hyderabad (via Police Action 'Operation Polo', Sept 1948), and Jammu & Kashmir (via Instrument of Accession signed by Maharaja Hari Singh on 26 Oct 1947); (2) Women of Bardoli conferred the title 'Sardar' on Patel during the Bardoli Satyagraha (1928); (3) Statue of Unity (182 m, Kevadia, Gujarat) honours Sardar Patel.
qe: Who is universally celebrated as the 'Iron Man of India' (भारत का लौह पुरुष) for successfully integrating over 560 princely states into the Indian Union after 1947?

q: भारत का संविधान किस तिथि को पूर्ण रूप से लागू हुआ, जिसे संप्रभु लोकतांत्रिक गणराज्य भारत के उदय के रूप में मनाया जाता है?
e: While adopted on 26 November 1949 (Constitution Day), the Constitution came into full force on 26 January 1950 to commemorate the historic 'Purna Swaraj' pledge of 26 January 1930 (Lahore Session, Dec 1929). (26 जनवरी 1930 के 'पूर्ण स्वराज' दिवस की स्मृति में भारतीय संविधान 26 जनवरी 1950 को पूर्णतः लागू हुआ।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Dr. Rajendra Prasad became India's first President and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar chaired the 7-member Drafting Committee; (2) Constituent Assembly took 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days to frame the Constitution; (3) On 24 January 1950, the National Anthem (*Jana Gana Mana*) and National Song (*Vande Mataram*) were adopted; (4) India's first General Elections were held in 1951–52 (Chief Election Commissioner: Sukumar Sen).
qe: On which date did the Constitution of India come into full force, marking the birth of the Sovereign Democratic Republic of India?

q: दिसंबर 1929 में जवाहरलाल नेहरू की अध्यक्षता वाले भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस के किस ऐतिहासिक अधिवेशन में 'पूर्ण स्वराज' का प्रस्ताव पारित किया गया?
e: The Lahore Session (December 1929, on the banks of the Ravi river) passed the Purna Swaraj resolution, hoisted the tricolour at midnight on 31 December 1929, and fixed 26 January 1930 as the first Independence Day. (दिसंबर 1929 के लाहौर अधिवेशन (अध्यक्ष: जवाहरलाल नेहरू) में पूर्ण स्वराज का प्रस्ताव पारित हुआ।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Karachi Session (March 1931, President: Sardar Patel) adopted the landmark resolution on Fundamental Rights and National Economic Programme; (2) Faizpur Session (Dec 1936, President: Nehru) was the first INC session held in a village; (3) Haripura (1938) & Tripuri (1939) sessions saw Subhas Chandra Bose elected President.
qe: At which historic Session of the Indian National Congress (December 1929), presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, was the resolution for 'Purna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) passed?

q: द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध में भारत को जबरन शामिल करने के विरोध में अक्टूबर 1940 में प्रारंभ हुए 'व्यक्तिगत सत्याग्रह' में महात्मा गांधी ने प्रथम सत्याग्रही किसे चुना?
e: On 17 October 1940 at Paunar (Maharashtra), Acharya Vinoba Bhave became the first Individual Satyagrahi, followed by Jawaharlal Nehru (second) and Brahma Dutt (third). (17 अक्टूबर 1940 को आचार्य विनोबा भावे प्रथम, जवाहरलाल नेहरू द्वितीय और ब्रह्मदत्त तृतीय व्यक्तिगत सत्याग्रही बने।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Individual Satyagraha was also called the 'Delhi Chalo Movement' and followed the rejection of the August Offer (1940); (2) Vinoba Bhave later launched the 'Bhoodan Movement' at Pochampally (Telangana) in April 1951; (3) He was the first Indian to win the Ramon Magsaysay Award (1958).
qe: Who was chosen by Mahatma Gandhi as the FIRST Individual Satyagrahi (October 1940) during the Individual Satyagraha Movement against India's forced participation in World War II?

q: 3 जून 1947 को घोषित किस संवैधानिक योजना के अंतर्गत ब्रिटिश भारत का भारत और पाकिस्तान नामक दो स्वतंत्र अधिराज्यों में विभाजन किया गया?
e: Viceroy Lord Mountbatten announced the 3rd June Plan (Mountbatten Plan), which was enacted by the British Parliament as the Indian Independence Act, 1947 (Royal Assent: 18 July 1947). (3 जून 1947 की माउंटबेटन योजना के आधार पर भारतीय स्वतंत्रता अधिनियम, 1947 पारित हुआ और विभाजन संपन्न हुआ।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Sir Cyril Radcliffe headed the two Boundary Commissions for Punjab and Bengal (Radcliffe Line); (2) Cabinet Mission (1946: Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps, A.V. Alexander) had rejected Partition and led to the formation of the Constituent Assembly; (3) C. Rajagopalachari was the first and only Indian Governor-General of Independent India (1948–50).
qe: Under which constitutional plan (announced on 3 June 1947) was the Partition of British India into two independent Dominions—India and Pakistan—carried out?

q: पोट्टी श्रीरामुलु के 56 दिनों के आमरण अनशन के पश्चात् 1 अक्टूबर 1953 को स्वतंत्र भारत का पहला भाषाई राज्य कौन-सा बना?
e: Created by separating Telugu-speaking districts from Madras State, Andhra State was inaugurated on 1 October 1953 (later expanded to Andhra Pradesh in 1956), leading to the appointment of the Fazl Ali Commission. (1 अक्टूबर 1953 को मद्रास से तेलुगु भाषी क्षेत्रों को अलग कर भारत का प्रथम भाषाई राज्य 'आंध्र राज्य' बनाया गया।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Earlier, Dhar Commission (1948) and JVP Committee (1948: Jawaharlal, Vallabhbhai, Pattabhi Sitaramayya) had cautioned against linguistic reorganization; (2) States Reorganisation Commission (Dec 1953) was chaired by Justice Fazl Ali with H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar; (3) The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (7th Constitutional Amendment) created 14 States and 6 Union Territories.
qe: Which state became the FIRST linguistic state of Independent India on 1 October 1953, following Potti Sriramulu's 56-day fast unto death?

q: प्रधानमंत्री जवाहरलाल नेहरू के अधीन स्वतंत्र भारत की विदेश नीति का आधारस्तंभ 'पंचशील समझौता' (29 अप्रैल 1954) भारत और किस देश के बीच हस्ताक्षरित हुआ था?
e: Signed on 29 April 1954 between India (Nehru) and China (Zhou Enlai) regarding Trade and Intercourse with Tibet, Panchsheel later shaped the 1955 Bandung Conference and the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM, 1961). (29 अप्रैल 1954 को भारत और चीन के बीच तिब्बत व्यापार समझौते की प्रस्तावना के रूप में पंचशील समझौता हुआ।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Five principles: Mutual respect for territorial integrity & sovereignty, Non-aggression, Non-interference in internal affairs, Equality & mutual benefit, Peaceful coexistence; (2) India's First Five-Year Plan (1951–56) focused on agriculture & irrigation (Bhakra Nangal, Hirakud), while Second Plan (1956–61, Mahalanobis Model) built Bhilai, Rourkela, and Durgapur steel plants.
qe: The 'Panchsheel Agreement' (Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence), a cornerstone of independent India's foreign policy under Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru, was signed on 29 April 1954 between India and:

q: 1951 में अंतरिम संसद द्वारा किस ऐतिहासिक संविधान संशोधन को पारित कर जमींदारी उन्मूलन व सामाजिक न्याय की रक्षा हेतु नौवीं अनुसूची, अनुच्छेद 31A, 31B और 15(4) जोड़े गए?
e: The First Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951 added the Ninth Schedule (shielding agrarian/land reform laws), inserted Article 15(4) (affirmative action for socially and educationally backward classes after *Champakam Dorairajan*), and added reasonable restrictions under Article 19(2). (प्रथम संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 1951 ने नौवीं अनुसूची, अनुच्छेद 31A, 31B और अनुच्छेद 15(4) जोड़े।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) The 7th Amendment Act, 1956 abolished the fourfold A/B/C/D classification of states and enabled common High Courts for two or more states; (2) The Hindu Code Bills were enacted as four major Acts in 1955–56 (Hindu Marriage Act 1955, Succession Act 1956, Minority & Guardianship Act 1956, Adoptions & Maintenance Act 1956).
qe: In 1951, which landmark Constitutional Amendment was passed by the Provisional Parliament—inserting the Ninth Schedule, Article 31A, Article 31B, and Article 15(4) to protect Zamindari abolition and social justice measures?

q:
गांधी-इरविन समझौते (5 मार्च 1931) के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: ब्रिटिश सरकार ने हिंसा के दोषी न पाए गए सभी राजनीतिक बंदियों को रिहा करने और तटीय निवासियों को निजी उपभोग हेतु नमक बनाने की अनुमति देना स्वीकार किया।
कथन II: इस समझौते में भगत सिंह, सुखदेव और राजगुरु की मृत्युदंड की सजा को आजीवन कारावास में बदलने का स्पष्ट प्रावधान था।
उपर्युक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?
o: कथन I और कथन II दोनों
न तो कथन I और न ही कथन II
e: Statement I is correct. Statement II is incorrect because Viceroy Lord Irwin rejected Gandhi's plea to commute the death sentences of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru (who were executed on 23 March 1931). (कथन I सही है; कथन II गलत है क्योंकि लॉर्ड इरविन ने भगत सिंह, सुखदेव व राजगुरु की फाँसी की सजा कम करने की माँग अस्वीकार कर दी थी।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Under the Pact, Congress agreed to suspend Civil Disobedience and attend the Second Round Table Conference; (2) Sarojini Naidu famously called Gandhi and Irwin the "Two Mahatmas" after the Pact.
qe:
Consider the following statements regarding the 'Gandhi-Irwin Pact' (5 March 1931):
Statement I: The British Government agreed to release all political prisoners not convicted of violence and permitted coastal residents to make salt for personal consumption.
Statement II: The Pact explicitly commuted the death sentences of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru to life imprisonment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
oe: Both Statement I and Statement II
Neither Statement I nor Statement II

q: नव-स्वतंत्र भारतीय गणराज्य (1950–1958) के निम्नलिखित संस्थानों/पहलों और उनके स्थापना वर्ष का कौन-सा युग्म सही सुमेलित नहीं है?
e: The University Grants Commission (UGC) became a statutory body under the UGC Act of **1956** (NOT 1958). All other three milestones of the 1950–58 Republic era are accurately matched. (UGC अधिनियम 1956 में पारित हुआ था, 1958 में नहीं; अन्य तीनों युग्म पूर्णतः सही हैं।) Exam Booster Facts: (1) Atomic Energy Commission was set up in 1948 (Dr. Homi J. Bhabha) and Department of Atomic Energy in 1954; India's first nuclear reactor 'Apsara' went critical in August 1956; (2) DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation) was established in **1958**; (3) Balwant Rai Mehta Committee submitted its 3-tier Panchayati Raj report in November 1957 (approved by NDC in January 1958).
qe: Which of the following institutions/initiatives of the newly independent Indian Republic (1950–1958) is NOT correctly matched with its year of establishment?

q:
सूची-I (1940 के दशक के संवैधानिक प्रस्ताव) को सूची-II (प्रमुख विशेषता / वर्ष) से सुमेलित कीजिए:
सूची-I: (1) अगस्त प्रस्ताव, (2) क्रिप्स मिशन, (3) कैबिनेट मिशन, (4) डिकी बर्ड प्लान (प्लान बाल्कन)
सूची-II: (a) त्रि-स्तरीय संघ व संविधान सभा का प्रस्ताव (1946), (b) भारतीयों द्वारा संविधान निर्माण की प्रथम स्पष्ट स्वीकृति (1940), (c) गांधीजी की 'पोस्ट-डेटेड चेक' टिप्पणी (1942), (d) माउंटबेटन का प्रारंभिक प्रारूप जिसे नेहरू ने अस्वीकार किया (मई 1947)
e: August Offer (8 Aug 1940, Lord Linlithgow) — 1-b; Cripps Mission (March 1942) — 2-c; Cabinet Mission (March–May 1946) — 3-a; Plan Balkan / Dickie Bird Plan (May 1947, proposing power transfer to individual provinces, rejected by Nehru at Shimla) — 4-d. q: द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना के दौरान "भारत का आर्थिक संविधान" कहे जाने वाले 1956 के औद्योगिक नीति संकल्प में भारतीय उद्योगों को कितनी अनुसूचियों (Schedules) में वर्गीकृत किया गया था?
o: तीन अनुसूचियाँ (अनुसूची A, B और C)
e: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 30 April 1956 (adopting the "Socialistic Pattern of Society" from the 1955 Avadi Congress Session) classified industries into 3 Schedules: Schedule A (17 core industries exclusively for Public Sector), Schedule B (12 progressively state-owned), and Schedule C (remaining left to Private Sector). qe: In the 1956 Industrial Policy Resolution—often called the "Economic Constitution of India" during the Second Five-Year Plan—Indian industries were classified into how many schedules?
oe: Three schedules (Schedule A, B, and C)
